name: Moth light
why: A new song in round 4's colours, in F on suspended chords: the hands, the marimba in sevens and one bell open it; the kick waits; your FM pluck bass grows from two notes to a line; a gated analog chord opens like a lamp coming up; a breakdown climbs a suspended rise without resolving, and the drop brings it all back together before it fades to embers. New here: the analog Deep kick, the warm pulse chord and the ring bell (↩ by a track's sound puts round 4's back).

sections.name: Moth light: Moths
sections.why: No kick: the hands thinned, one bell every four bars, the marimba's seven-step loop drifting against the bar.

sections.name: Moth light: Lamplight
sections.why: A few closed hats; twigs join the hands; the bell rises to a second and third note.

sections.name: Moth light: Wingbeat
sections.why: Onto eleven and six: the kick on one and three, the drummer's hats, and the bass: just two notes on the and. The marimba has moved a note.

sections.name: Moth light: Flutter
sections.why: The bass developed over four bars, the hands answering with a bamboo fill, the marimba back with a step added; the bell rests; the chord brighter.

sections.name: Moth light: Glass
sections.why: The breakdown: no kick, no bass; a suspended rise that never resolves, the chord's filter opening bar by bar, the hats rising into the drop.

sections.name: Moth light: Swarm
sections.why: The drop: the bass's whole line, the chord as stabs in fives pumping on the kick, the bell and the marimba together for the first time.

sections.name: Moth light: Embers
sections.why: The kick thins, the bass in long notes fading, the chord closing, one bell, the marimba as it began.
